name: Thompson Zihuatanejo
positioning: Beachfront resort on Playa La Ropa in Bahia de Zihuatanejo, near Ixtapa, with mid-century design using local materials and many suites with private plunge pools
best_for: Couples who want a suite with a private plunge pool on the beach
Travelers who care about wood-fired and modern Mexican cooking

facts.text: The resort is a beachfront hotel on Playa La Ropa in Bahia de Zihuatanejo.
The resort sits on what was once a secluded fishing village near Ixtapa.
Rooms and suites face garden, lagoon or ocean views.
Rooms and suites are designed with a mid-century aesthetic using materials and textures indigenous to Playa La Ropa.
Ceniza serves a sustainably sourced menu of Mexican surf and turf dishes.
On Thursdays, Hao holds a grill-out of seafood and meats grilled oceanside with live music.
On Saturdays, Hao hosts a beachfront taco experience with handmade rolled tortillas.
The resort has two tennis courts, with racquets and balls provided.
The fitness center is surrounded by tropical gardens and has Peloton bikes.
The spa is set with Moroccan-style lanterns and the sound of the ocean breeze.
The hotel offers cooking classes and tequila tastings, and guests can go parasailing and jet-skiing.
The hotel was formerly the Viceroy, and Tides.

highlights.text: Ceniza, named for the Spanish word for ash, puts a spin on traditional wood-fired cooking under a palm-thatched palapa.
La Parota is the resort's 'Dinner in the Wild', where smoke is the base for all dishes.
Several suites have a private plunge pool on the terrace or balcony, and the two-bedroom Thompson Suite has direct beach access.
Rooms feature deep amber parotta woods, Oaxacan clay light fixtures, brass details and Mexican artwork.
Hao is an oceanfront all-day bar serving seasonal ingredients in modern Mexican style.

considerations.text: Ixtapa-Zihuatanejo International Airport is 8 miles away, and the hotel can arrange private airport transfers.
A daily guest amenity fee is applied to each room.
Self-parking at the hotel entrance is free for registered guests, but space is limited.
